scenario: A first-time interchangeable-lens-camera buyer is considering a coworker's roughly decade-old body and wants to know whether putting the same money toward a newer generation would materially improve ordinary family photography. The frozen seller corpus contains three older DSLR-era paths and three 2018 full-frame mirrorless paths, but these are unlike listings rather than a controlled test. Nikon's D7000 renewed kit page lists 799 dollars with no posted review, a 16.2MP DX CMOS sensor, six frames per second and an 18-105mm lens. Canon's EOS 7D kit page lists 899.55 dollars, a 100-percent rating over eight reviews, an 18MP APS-C sensor, nineteen AF points, eight frames per second and an 18-135mm stabilized lens. Sony's A300 body page lists 337.99 dollars with no posted review, a 10.2MP APS-C CCD, body-based stabilization and a body-only configuration. The Sony a7 III bundle lists 1,999 dollars, a 100-percent rating over two reviews, a 24.2MP full-frame sensor, ten frames per second and accessory bundle language. The Nikon Z6 bundle lists 1,728 dollars with no posted review, a 24.5MP BSI full-frame sensor, 273-point phase-detect AF, five-axis sensor-shift stabilization and an FTZ adapter. The Canon EOS R bundle lists 1,869 dollars with no posted review, a 30.3MP full-frame sensor, Dual Pixel AF, 5,655 selectable AF points, an electronic viewfinder and an EF-to-RF adapter. Model pages place the D7000 and 7D in 2010 and 2009, and the a7 III, Z6 and EOS R in 2018, so seller 'Date First Available' fields cannot be substituted for launch generation. General sources describe BSI, CMOS development, stabilization, EVF preview, rolling-shutter distortion and dynamic range. Community discussions contain both a used-prosumer recommendation and a warning that beginners can miss used defects, show substantial improvement with retained core gear plus practice and processing changes, and show a newer phone failing an older phone's close-focus expectation because the lens and mode set changed. None of these sources measures the coworker's physical unit or supplies a matched family-photo comparison of the six listings.
target: Determine what the six frozen seller pages and five matching model histories actually establish about exact offer identity, condition, price, review sample, lens or bundle completeness, release generation and nominal sensor, autofocus, stabilization, viewfinder, shutter and workflow capabilities. Explain which changes have a plausible mechanism for daylight portraits, dim stationary interiors, moving children or pets, close subjects and short handheld video, and which are merely feature counts or marketing until measured. Keep BSI, CMOS evolution, AF coverage and tracking, camera-shake stabilization, EVF preview, rolling readout and dynamic range distinct, and keep each community statement at its author, unit, lens, subject, skill and processing scope. End with a physical used-unit inspection and native-file gate, equivalent complete-kit pricing, a small matched and preferably blinded family-photo trial with predeclared keeper-rate, blur, noise, highlight, close-focus, skew, stability, battery, handling and workflow thresholds, a repeatability and confound check, and an incremental-value procedure that buys only the lowest-cost complete passing path or borrows, rents, keeps the current phone or defers.
